tags.inscription: Abergavenny was known for its flannel, a fine soft woollen cloth. Here was the site of a flannel mill in the 18th century.
tags.name: Flannel Street

tags.description: Henry VIII founded the grammar school here. He gave the old parish church, St John's, to house the school and granted some of the taxes (the tithes) of the closed down priory to pay for it.
tags.name: King Henry VIII Grammar School 1542-1898

tags.description: In the 18th century most wealthy and professional men wore wigs. For a time, Abergavenny was known for its fashionable white periwigs made of goat hair, sometimes sold at 40 guineas each.
tags.inscription: Abergavenny was known for the manufacture of white periwigs. On this side lived James Jones, hair bleacher circa 1741. A method of bleaching the hair is said to have been invented in the town.
tags.name: Periwig Makers
